title: Merkle Trees as Recursive Defect Localization
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in distributed systems/cryptographic data structures, centered on the claim that hierarchical commitments summarize bounded regions and disagreement is localized by recursively descending only defective boundaries. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that synchronization cost falls by preserving recursive witness structure. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: small tree, single-leaf mutation, and comparison path.

title: Consistent Hashing as Low-Defect Boundary Migration
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in distributed systems, centered on the claim that ownership boundaries move under topology change while minimizing reassignment of unaffected objects. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that rebalancing quality can be viewed as migration defect under boundary motion. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: ring example, node addition/removal, and moved-key count.

title: Transactions and ACID as Distinct Closure Obligations
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in database systems, centered on the claim that transaction execution creates temporary transformation boundaries and commit requires declared closure conditions. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that atomicity consistency isolation durability become separable operational obligations. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: two-transaction schedule, isolation anomaly, and rollback/commit trace.

title: CAP as Competing Closure Obligations under Partition
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in distributed systems, centered on the claim that network partition breaks communication closure and forces a choice between globally consistent observation and local service continuity. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that CAP states which closure obligation remains authoritative when coordination fails. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: two-replica partition trace, consistency choice, and availability choice.

title: Quorum Consensus as Witness Continuity
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in distributed consensus, centered on the claim that quorum intersection preserves a witness path between successive decisions. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that majority overlap prevents decision histories from becoming informationally disjoint. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: quorum intersection arithmetic, toy consensus trace, and non-intersecting counterexample.

title: CRDTs as Lawful Local Divergence with Guaranteed Reclosure
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in distributed data types, centered on the claim that replicas may diverge locally while merge laws keep all states inside a closure-guaranteeing space. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that temporary representation divergence is separated from semantic inconsistency. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: G-counter or OR-set, concurrent updates, and merge convergence.

title: Caching and Invalidation as Representation Authority
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in systems/software architecture, centered on the claim that a cache is a detached representation whose authority depends on dependency-preserving update/invalidation boundaries. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that staleness is representational defect and invalidation is coherence repair. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: cache/source trace, stale read, and invalidation repair.

title: Hoare Logic and Contracts as Boundary Obligations
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in program verification, centered on the claim that preconditions define admissible entry, postconditions required exit, invariants what must survive transport. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that contracts become typed boundary obligations across execution. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: simple Hoare triple, loop invariant, and failing precondition.

title: Behavioral Subtyping as Admissible Replacement
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in type systems/software design, centered on the claim that replacement is lawful only when all obligations exposed by the original interface boundary remain satisfiable. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that substitutability becomes obligation-preserving transport across an interface. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: valid subtype and strengthened-precondition counterexample.

title: Undecidability as a Boundary on Mechanically Available Distinctions
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in computability, centered on the claim that some distinctions about arbitrary executions cannot be uniformly decided by an effective procedure. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that boundary language must respect rather than evade classical undecidability. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: halting reduction, Rice theorem statement, and claim firewall.

title: Software Design Patterns as Boundary Transformations
summary: This paper candidate develops “Software Design Patterns as Boundary Transformations” from material already present in the Lab corpus. Its current claim ceiling is this is a direct precursor to the Lab's later software-pattern and ontology/runtime work and can be rewritten as a conservative CS interpretation paper using Adapter/Facade/Proxy/Observer/Decorator/Factory as typed examples. The current artifact state is legacy manuscript candidate re-routed through current publication controls. The next evidence obligation is pattern catalog as boundary-transform vocabulary; adapter as representation-preserving boundary transform; facade as coarse boundary readout; observer as controlled information exposure. Prior to promotion, it requires review against pattern-by-pattern native definition, preservation/forgetting obligation, counterexample or misuse case, explicit no-new-mathematics ceiling.

title: Accessibility Equivalence for Spatial and Semantic Navigation Interfaces
summary: This paper candidate develops “Accessibility Equivalence for Spatial and Semantic Navigation Interfaces” from material already present in the Lab corpus. Its current claim ceiling is accessibility design/evaluation result; equivalence must be operationally defined rather than asserted. The current artifact state is explicit doctrine requirement and named empirical evaluation. The next evidence obligation is define semantic-task equivalence and compare spatial, keyboard, screen-reader and non-spatial projections with participants using relevant access modalities. Prior to promotion, it requires review against accessible visualization, non-visual graph navigation, keyboard interaction, screen-reader interfaces, reduced motion, WCAG and equivalent facilitation.

title: Invariant-Preserving Compression and Recall After Detail Exploration
summary: This paper candidate develops “Invariant-Preserving Compression and Recall After Detail Exploration” from material already present in the Lab corpus. Its current claim ceiling is empirical memory/comprehension result plus bounded interface formalization. The current artifact state is explicit H3 hypothesis with candidate invariant law. The next evidence obligation is structured-summary versus visual-retreat baseline; recall of high-level relations, contradictions and provenance after exploration. Prior to promotion, it requires review against aggregation in visualization, semantic zoom, summarization, overview-detail, cognitive maps, recall and information compression.

title: Reframing Without Losing the Object: Identity Persistence Across Coordinated System Views
summary: This paper candidate develops “Reframing Without Losing the Object: Identity Persistence Across Coordinated System Views” from material already present in the Lab corpus. Its current claim ceiling is interaction-design synthesis and comparative user-study result. The current artifact state is signature mechanic with explicit empirical evaluation target. The next evidence obligation is comparison accuracy, object-identification errors, state-transfer errors and orientation under multiple projections. Prior to promotion, it requires review against coordinated multiple views, brushing and linking, object constancy, animated transitions, cognitive continuity, model-view architectures and comparative visualization.
